brand.tagline: Finding Jesus in the whole Bible, one panel at a time. Every encounter, every prophecy, every promise.
brand.mission: Awakeden is about finding Jesus in the whole Bible, Old Testament and New, the same Lord in both. He is the thread running through all of it: the encounters, the prophecies, the promises kept. Every piece is hand-inked and filmed panel by panel, with the Scripture in red and quoted exactly (KJV). Watch each one as a short film, sit with the longer ones, or read the whole study right here. Some series focus on one window: the Old Testament, His miracles, the questions He asked, the people who met Him. Serious about the Bible. Clear about the gospel. Made to draw you in, not wear you down. The ink is ours. The words are His.

items.title: Isaiah 53: The Suffering Servant
items.public_hook: Seven hundred years before the cross, Isaiah wrote of a wound that would heal ours.
items.public_blurb: Long-form on Isaiah 53. The Suffering Servant, wounded for our transgressions, fulfilled in the New Testament. The first Awakeden deep-dive slated for release.

items.title: Psalm 22: The Song From the Cross
items.public_hook: David wrote the crucifixion a thousand years before Rome nailed anyone to a cross.
items.public_blurb: One locked long-form study on Psalm 22, cut into eight gospel shorts. Each short follows one beat from the psalm Jesus lived out on the cross.

items.title: The Forsaken Cry
items.public_hook: The loneliest line Jesus spoke from the cross was a quote from Psalm 22.
items.public_blurb: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? David wrote it. Jesus cried it from the cross.

items.title: The Crucifixion Foretold
items.public_hook: Ten centuries before the cross, a psalm said a dying man's clothes would be divided.
items.public_blurb: Psalm 22:18. They part my garments and cast lots. John records the soldiers doing exactly that.

items.title: Father, Forgive Them
items.public_hook: The first word from the cross is a prayer for the men driving the nails.
items.public_blurb: Luke 23:34. While the soldiers divided his garments, Jesus prayed forgiveness over them. The first word from the cross, drawn panel by panel.

items.title: The Mockers' Words
items.public_hook: The crowd mocked Him. They repeated words David had written a thousand years earlier.
items.public_blurb: David wrote the mockers' gesture and their taunt. Matthew records both at the cross.

items.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver
items.public_hook: Zechariah priced the betrayal five hundred years early: thirty pieces of silver, thrown down in the house of the LORD.
items.public_blurb: Zechariah 11:12-13 names the price, the contempt, and the temple floor. Judas fulfilled every word of it. The prophecy that priced the Messiah.

items.title: Today in Paradise
items.public_hook: Two thieves. Same cross. Two answers.
items.public_blurb: Luke 23:39-43. One thief railed, one asked to be remembered, and Jesus answered with a promise dated TODAY. The second word from the cross.

items.title: Declared to the Brethren
items.public_hook: The psalm moves from forsaken to declaring God's name to the congregation.
items.public_blurb: Psalm 22:22. I will declare thy name unto my brethren. Hebrews applies it to the risen Christ.

items.title: Woman, Behold Thy Son
items.public_hook: Simeon promised Mary a sword. At the cross, Jesus watched it land, and gave her a son.
items.public_blurb: Luke 2:35 meets John 19:26-27. The sword Simeon foretold pierces Mary at Golgotha, and the dying Jesus binds her wound with a son and a home.

items.title: He Hath Done This
items.public_hook: It is finished. The psalm said He would declare it to a people yet unborn.
items.public_blurb: The closing line of Psalm 22, that he hath done this, lands on Christ's finished work.

items.title: It Is Finished
items.public_hook: The first time the Bible says finished, nothing was broken yet.
items.public_blurb: Genesis 2:1 and John 19:30. Two finished works, one Workman: He finished creation and rested; He finished redemption and rose. Enter his rest.

items.title: The Ends of the Earth
items.public_hook: All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the Lord.
items.public_blurb: Psalm 22:27. The nations turning to worship, fulfilled through Christ.

items.title: Father, Into Thy Hands
items.public_hook: A dying man's last words. And they were a child's bedtime prayer.
items.public_blurb: Psalm 31:5 was an evening prayer a child could learn. Luke 23:46: with his last breath Jesus prayed it, and added one word: Father.

items.title: The Body Foretold
items.public_hook: I am poured out like water. David described a body the cross would fulfil.
items.public_blurb: Poured out, bones out of joint, hands and feet pierced. The psalm's language fits the crucifixion.

items.title: Could Ye Not Watch One Hour
items.public_hook: Jesus asked three fishermen for one thing. They failed inside an hour.
items.public_blurb: Matthew 26:36-46. Gethsemane, the cup, the sleeping disciples, and the mercy in the question. He watched that hour alone so no hour of yours is watched alone.

items.title: I Thirst
items.public_hook: Two words from the cross. David wrote the thirst a thousand years before.
items.public_blurb: My tongue cleaveth to my jaws. The psalm's thirst, fulfilled in Jesus' cry from the cross.

items.title: The One They Pierced
items.public_hook: A Roman soldier drove a spear into a dead man's side to be sure He was gone. He had no idea he was finishing a sentence God wrote five centuries earlier.
items.public_blurb: Zechariah 12:10. The LORD says they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, then mourn for him as for an only son. John cites it at the spear. The pierced one is God himself, the Son. Look at Him and live.

items.title: Why Are You Afraid?
items.public_hook: The disciples were drowning.
items.public_blurb: The disciples were drowning.

items.title: Psalm 22, Part 2
items.public_hook: What if part of Jesus' story was written before it happened?
items.public_blurb: What if part of Jesus' story was written before it happened?

items.title: He Said It Under the Lamps
items.public_hook: At the Feast of Tabernacles, they lit four giant lamps in the temple, and that's when Jesus said this.
items.public_blurb: At the Feast of Tabernacles, they lit four giant lamps in the temple, and that's when Jesus said this.

items.title: I AM the Light of the World
items.public_hook: They lit four giant fires in the temple that night to remember when God led them. Then Jesus stood up and claimed to be the fire.
items.public_blurb: They lit four giant fires in the temple that night to remember when God led them. Then Jesus stood up and claimed to be the fire.

items.title: I AM the Door: The Shepherd Who Became the Gate
items.public_hook: In ancient Israel, the shepherd was the door. Literally his body.
items.public_blurb: In ancient Israel, the shepherd was the door. Literally his body.

items.title: The Well That Never Runs Dry
items.public_hook: She came to the well at noon to avoid the whispers. Five husbands behind her, a sixth man at home, and a thirst nothing had touched.
items.public_blurb: She came to the well at noon to avoid the whispers. Five husbands behind her, a sixth man at home, and a thirst nothing had touched.

items.title: The Father Who Ran
items.public_hook: We call it the parable of the prodigal son. But the son walks home slow and filthy. The only one running is the father.
items.public_blurb: We call it the parable of the prodigal son. But the son walks home slow and filthy. The only one running is the father.

items.title: The Line He Never Got to Say
items.public_hook: He rehearsed three lines on the road home. He only got to say two. Read it again, the third sentence is gone.
items.public_blurb: He rehearsed three lines on the road home. He only got to say two. Read it again, the third sentence is gone.

items.title: The Confession He Never Finished
items.public_hook: He rehearsed his apology the whole way home. Three parts. He only got two of them out, and that changes everything.
items.public_blurb: He rehearsed his apology the whole way home. Three parts. He only got two of them out, and that changes everything.

items.title: The Kiss That Cut Off the Bargain
items.public_hook: He rehearsed the speech the whole walk home. Three lines. He only got to deliver two, the kiss cut off the third.
items.public_blurb: He rehearsed the speech the whole walk home. Three lines. He only got to deliver two, the kiss cut off the third.

items.title: The Fire Jesus Built
items.public_hook: The last time Peter smelled charcoal smoke, he was denying Jesus by a fire. The risen Christ has built him another.
items.public_blurb: The last time Peter smelled charcoal smoke, he was denying Jesus by a fire. The risen Christ has built him another.

items.title: He Never Said Yes
items.public_hook: Bethesda meant "House of Mercy", and it was the most merciless place in Jerusalem. For thirty-eight years one man lay there, too crippled to ever reach the water first.
items.public_blurb: Bethesda meant "House of Mercy", and it was the most merciless place in Jerusalem. For thirty-eight years one man lay there, too crippled to ever reach the water first.

items.title: The Cliff of Rival Gods
items.public_hook: A cliffside honeycombed with pagan shrines. Pan's grotto behind Him. Caesar's white temple gleaming above. And Jesus picks THIS rock to ask the question.
items.public_blurb: A cliffside honeycombed with pagan shrines. Pan's grotto behind Him. Caesar's white temple gleaming above. And Jesus picks THIS rock to ask the question.

items.title: He Was Asleep in the Storm
items.public_hook: Waves breaking over the rail. Water in the boat past your knees. Men screaming for their lives. And in the stern, He is asleep.
items.public_blurb: Waves breaking over the rail. Water in the boat past your knees. Men screaming for their lives. And in the stern, He is asleep.

items.title: The Pronouns That Preached the Gospel
items.public_hook: You think your failure disqualifies you. The man who denied Jesus to his face wrote the sentence that heals you, and it pivots on pronouns.
items.public_blurb: You think your failure disqualifies you. The man who denied Jesus to his face wrote the sentence that heals you, and it pivots on pronouns.

items.title: He Never Answered Jesus
items.public_hook: Thirty-eight years on a mat. Jesus asks one question. And here is the detail almost everyone misses, the man never answers it. He explains why he can't.
items.public_blurb: Thirty-eight years on a mat. Jesus asks one question. And here is the detail almost everyone misses, the man never answers it. He explains why he can't.

items.title: The Prepared Belly
items.public_hook: You remember Jonah swallowed by a fish. Open the chapter, he is the man thrown overboard so the rest of the ship could live.
items.public_blurb: You remember Jonah swallowed by a fish. Open the chapter, he is the man thrown overboard so the rest of the ship could live.

items.title: The Answer Was a Gift
items.public_hook: Before He asks His real question, Jesus takes a poll. He doesn't start with you. He starts with the crowd, what does everyone out there say about Him?
items.public_blurb: Before He asks His real question, Jesus takes a poll. He doesn't start with you. He starts with the crowd, what does everyone out there say about Him?

items.title: The Question on the Gaza Road
items.public_hook: Seven hundred years before the cross, a Jewish prophet described a death like it, and on the Gaza road, an African official is reading that scroll aloud.
items.public_blurb: Seven hundred years before the cross, a Jewish prophet described a death like it, and on the Gaza road, an African official is reading that scroll aloud.

items.title: Jesus Walked Past the Pool
items.public_hook: For thirty-eight years he waited for the water to stir. Jesus walked past the water, and stopped at him.
items.public_blurb: For thirty-eight years he waited for the water to stir. Jesus walked past the water, and stopped at him.

items.title: A List of Dead Men
items.public_hook: You've already filed Jesus, great teacher, historical figure, the faith you left in childhood. Then He turns from the crowd and asks one question.

items.title: What Manner of Man
items.public_hook: Black water pours over the rail, seasoned sailors screaming for their lives, and in the stern, soaked and rocking, one man is sound asleep.
items.public_blurb: Black water pours over the rail, seasoned sailors screaming for their lives, and in the stern, soaked and rocking, one man is sound asleep.

items.title: The Race He Could Never Win
items.public_hook: Five porches packed with the blind and the lame, all staring at one pool. When the water stirs, only the first one in is healed.
items.public_blurb: Five porches packed with the blind and the lame, all staring at one pool. When the water stirs, only the first one in is healed.

items.title: Smitten of God
items.public_hook: Watch the crucifixion through the crowd's eyes, and you'll read it exactly the way they did: a man getting what God decided he deserved.

items.title: The Light You Can Stand In
items.public_hook: Stones drop in the dust, one by one. The accusers file out, oldest first, leaving one accused woman alone with Jesus in the light.
items.public_blurb: Stones drop in the dust, one by one. The accusers file out, oldest first, leaving one accused woman alone with Jesus in the light.

items.title: The Door Was a Body
items.public_hook: God's own name is "I AM", too holy to speak. And God looked at people who could never reach Him, and opened a door.

items.public_hook: Out in the hills, a sheepfold often had no gate, just a gap in the stones. At night the shepherd lay across it, his body the door.

items.public_hook: You can be completely full and still feel empty. Fridge stocked, day went fine, and something deeper than your stomach is still hungry.

items.public_hook: In the desert, God rained bread from heaven each morning. They gathered it, ate, lived another day, and still, every one died.

items.title: In No Wise Cast Out
items.public_hook: Somewhere in you is the quiet fear that if you actually came to God, He'd look at your record and turn you away.
